requirements.requirement: /srv/drop exists as a shared writable directory on node1
requirements.summary: Directory created with mode 1777, owned root:root (world-writable), confirmed via stat both immediately after creation and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users in /srv/drop (sticky bit enforcement)
requirements.summary: Two test users created; user B successfully wrote a file but failed to delete user A's file (Operation not permitted, exit 1), while each user could delete their own file (exit 0). Re-verified with fresh test users after reboot with identical results.

requirements.requirement: Configuration persists across a restart of node1
requirements.summary: tmpfiles.d rule written for /srv/drop; a real reboot was performed (boot_id changed from be303eb3... to 23fd1542...), and both the directory permissions and sticky-bit enforcement were independently re-verified post-reboot, directly confirming the healthy baseline, the disruption, and recovered functional state.

overall_summary: The executor fully satisfied the task: /srv/drop was created with mode 1777 root:root, sticky-bit enforcement preventing cross-user file deletion was functionally demonstrated both before and after a genuine node reboot (boot_id changed), and persistence was configured via /etc/tmpfiles.d and confirmed to survive the restart. The same reboot cycle also satisfies the provider-wide restart evidence protocol, showing pre-restart healthy state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered configuration/functional state. Hygiene is very good, with only a trivial leftover log file from the reboot command.
limitations: The /tmp/reboot.log file left behind after the reboot was not explicitly cleaned up, though it is a benign artifact of a sanctioned action.
No other managed nodes existed in this topology (only node1), so the restart evidence protocol scope is limited to node1 by design, not by executor gap.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task requirements: directory creation/permissioning, temporary test users created and fully removed twice (cmd-130df3fb785441f4/cmd-722db62835aa4ff5 paired with userdel calls in cmd-e0ecd9e34d8e4dfe and within cmd-722db62835aa4ff5), tmpfiles.d persistence rule, and a single reboot used both to satisfy persistence verification and to serve as the provider-wide restart evidence protocol. No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were found. The only minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log, an artifact of the backgrounded nohup reboot command (cmd-2a2c7fa2c5fe416b) visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot; it is low-risk, non-sensitive, and directly tied to the sanctioned reboot action, so it only marginally reduces the hygiene score.
